negative_findings.description: None of the aggregators (Clarity Project, Opendatabot, YouControl, VKURSI) surfaced a ready-made banking/payments or ATM/POS vertical view in search results — no 'банкомати' or 'платіжні термінали' landing page, category or curated supplier list was found.
negative_findings.result_summary: Sector slicing must be constructed by us via CPV filters and KVED codes on top of generic company/tender search; no vendor offers a payments-industry cut off the shelf.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design cannot rely on a vendor-provided sector segment; we must own the CPV/KVED taxonomy that defines 'UA banking & payments technology supplier'.

negative_findings.description: The CPV code used in the seed exploration for ATMs (30160000, taken from the query formulation) was not confirmed against an authoritative CPV/ДК 021:2015 listing during this run.
negative_findings.result_summary: No source found in this run that states the exact ДК 021:2015 codes for ATMs, POS terminals, processing services or banking software.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The whole supplier-enumeration approach hinges on the correct CPV set; an unverified code would silently truncate the supplier universe.

negative_findings.description: The AMCU 'Державний реєстр суб'єктів господарювання, притягнутих до відповідальності' was confirmed to exist via an AMCU news page and third-party commentary, but the direct register URL / dataset endpoint was not located in this run.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only the announcement page and secondary explainers were captured; the register's own address remains to be found on the AMCU site.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The blacklist is a key screening feed; without a stable endpoint it cannot be automated.

negative_findings.description: Licensing and bulk-use terms for Clarity Project, YouControl and VKURSI were not read in this run; only pricing/feature pages were surfaced for Opendatabot and VKURSI.
negative_findings.result_summary: Whether systematic extraction is contractually permitted (vs. requiring an API/enterprise plan) is unresolved for the three most useful aggregators.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Determines whether these become automated feeds or manual-lookup tools; scraping against ToS is a legal and continuity risk.

negative_findings.description: EDR open-data publication has been interrupted and only partly restored (reported January 2026), with defence-sector, arms-manufacturer and strategic-facility entries kept closed.
negative_findings.result_summary: Ownership/UBO coverage is incomplete by design for some entities; state-bank-adjacent or dual-use suppliers may be missing or thinned.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any beneficial-ownership map built now has known blind spots that must be declared in downstream analysis.

coverage_gaps.description: No verified CPV (ДК 021:2015) code set for ATMs, POS/payment terminals, card personalisation, processing services, core banking and cash-handling equipment.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pull the official ДК 021:2015 classifier and pin the exact code list; validate by sampling known banking tenders in BI Prozorro and checking their CPV.

coverage_gaps.description: No named UA banking/payments vendor entities (with EDRPOU) were captured in this run — the supplier universe is still empty, only the machinery to build it was mapped.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run the BI Prozorro Suppliers sheet and Prozorro API awards feed over the pinned CPV set to extract the initial EDRPOU list, then hydrate each via Clarity/YouControl.

coverage_gaps.description: Private-bank (non-state) procurement is largely out of Prozorro scope, so aggregator tender history covers state and state-bank buyers only; commercial-bank vendor relationships are invisible in this cell.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pair this cell with non-tender sources (vendor press releases, bank annual reports, NBU registers of payment infrastructure operators) to cover private-sector demand.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a targeted pass on NAZK/NSDC sanctions registers and their open-data endpoints as a supplier-screening layer.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Let the deterministic liveness pass verify; re-check the AMCU deep links and bi.prozorro.org root in particular, since deep AMCU paths change with site restructuring.

brief: For Ukraine, tender history is effectively a solved data-join problem: Prozorro carries the supplier's EDRPOU under the 'UA-EDR' identifier scheme, and a layer of commercial aggregators — Clarity Project, YouControl, VKURSI.PRO (Tender BI) and Opendatabot — joins that key to the state company register to produce vendor pages listing every tender a firm bid on, its buyers, competitors and owners. That makes supplier-first enumeration of the UA banking/payments technology market feasible: pull the supplier population from the free official BI Prozorro 'Постачальники' sheet or the OpenProcurement API by CPV, then hydrate each EDRPOU through the aggregators, cross-check payment reality on Є-Data/spending.gov.ua and screen against the AMCU bid-rigging lists and blacklist. Two structural caveats bound the cell: none of the platforms offers a ready-made banking/payments vertical, so the CPV/KVED taxonomy is ours to define and verify; and EDR open data is only partly restored under martial law, with defence and strategic entities withheld, so beneficial-ownership coverage has declared blind spots. Free official sources (BI Prozorro, Prozorro API, data.gov.ua EDR, AMCU, Є-Data) should carry the automated backbone, with the commercial aggregators used for affiliation mapping and targeted lookups under their own licence terms.
